title: VIP culture in hospitals can compromise patient safety: Aiims doctors
description:
Preferential treatment for influential individuals can compromise patient safety and equitable access to healthcare, AIIMS Delhi doctors said, suggesting institutional discussions on uniform policies to safeguard equity in patient care.
Pressure from patients or hospital administrators to divert scarce hospital resources can also lead to avoidable complications, Dr M D Ray, Professor of Surgical Oncology at AIIMS, Delhi, and his MCh student Dr Hema Siri Kottu said in an article published in Oncology Reviews.
The doctors examined the ethical and clinical challenges posed by what is known as "VIP syndrome" -- influential patients receiving preferential treatment while deviating from standard medical protocols in resource-constrained settings.
"While special accommodations for high-profile individuals may be acceptable if they do not compromise access or the quality of care for others, healthcare providers must be vigilant," the authors stated.
